alignments.note: Adversative μέντοι rendered by the ASV's clause-initial *Howbeit*; its own aligned unit under rule 2, separate from the conditional particle. Rule 39 is not in question (no fusion with a negative), and rule 65 is the shape: a particle standing beside a conditional is decided on its own English word. μέντοι is a distinct lexeme, not the correlative μέν of rule 70.
Ordinary conditional εἰ → *if* under rule 40's clause-introducer principle.
Inflected 2pl verb takes its supplied English subject under rules 7 and 9, headed on the lexical verb *fulfil* rather than on *ye*.
νόμον and βασιλικόν are both anarthrous, so rule 58 gives the supplied determiner to the noun, discontinuously under rule 15: *the … law* here and a bare *royal* to the adjective.
Attributive adjective keeps only *royal*; the determiner is the noun's under rule 58.

κατά → *according to* as one contiguous multiword prepositional expression, headed on the meaning-bearing *according* under rule 17; *to* is the idiom's own particle, not the case preposition, so the following article keeps a bare *the* under rule 21. Rule 67 is not in question: no supplied noun stands in this frame, and rule 78's *for … sake* wrap is discontinuous where this is not.
Noun stands alone, its determiner having gone to the article under rule 21.
Future indicative with supplied subject and auxiliary; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb *love*.

Article displaced by the possessive under rule 20: the genitive σου is present and, by rule 76's availability test, free — its only English is *thy* — so it carries the possessive and the article realizes nothing.

Substantivized adverb πλησίον → *neighbor*. The competing reading would treat τὸν πλησίον as rule 49's `τὸ τρίτον` → *the part*, with the article taking a supplied nominal; it does not hold, because *neighbor* is the corpus gloss of πλησίον itself under rule 91's operational test rather than a generic completion supplied for the article, and the determiner slot is already σου's under rule 20.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive *thy*, which is what empties the article under rule 20.
Comparative ὡς → *as*; no correlative καί follows, so rule 82 is not in question.

Inflected verb with supplied subject, headed on the lexical *do* under rules 9 and 17. Split from καλῶς rather than merged into a *do well* unit: the ASV writes a word for each token, so rule 2 applies and rule 73's collapsed light-verb case does not.

Adverb καλῶς → *well*, its own unit; the ASV's reordering is immaterial under rule 15. Rule 85 records the same collocation at TIT/2CO-style `καλῶς ποιεῖτε` → *ye do well that…*, likewise splitting verb from adverb.

review_notes: Reviewed and kept unchanged in structure: all sixteen units of the accepted alignment stand. Only the notes on s006, s010 and s011 were extended to record the competing readings a later reader would otherwise have to re-derive.
Partition checked: every s### and t### id appears exactly once; 16 source and 21 target tokens.

The only unrepresented unit is s010 τόν, emptied by the free genitive σου under rule 20's proper case (and rule 76's availability test, σου spending nothing else). A reference comparison may report it as a disagreement; that report is not a correction.

κατά takes *according to* whole and τήν keeps a bare *the*. Reading *to* as the case preposition riding on the article under rule 21 is the defensible alternative, but *according to* is one English preposition and splitting it would leave *according* bare; the head stays on *according* as the meaning-bearing word under rule 17, not on *to* by analogy with rule 78's *for … sake*, which is a discontinuous wrap around a supplied noun and not this construction.
s003 νόμον carries the discontinuous *the … law* under rule 58 because both noun and adjective are anarthrous; the competing reading giving *the* to *royal* by word order is what rule 58 forbids.

τὸν πλησίον σου was audited separately as the verse's one genuinely open article: the article substantivizes an adverb, so rule 49's supplied-nominal case (`τὸ τρίτον` → *the part*) is the reading to rule out. It is ruled out because *neighbor* glosses πλησίον itself under rule 91 and the determiner slot is already occupied by σου, leaving the article nothing.

εἰ μέντοι is kept as two units. Rule 39's noncompositional cluster is scoped to a particle fused with the negative μή, and rule 65 decides an accompanying particle on its own English word; the ASV writes one here (*Howbeit*), so both are aligned.
